charter:
# Charter — S00 usage inventory (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** S00 'Usage inventory → parity/parity.yaml', track v1, ADM phase G, tranche 0, project `01a1d039-0d26-7573-9b0c-e0f60af92003`, plan `docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md`. The row records `status: closed`, `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]`, `meta.closure_outputs: []` and no issues. It was reopened for the #526 retrospective rework under delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Mandate:** measure from durable and sampled evidence which fr, RM, Planka and n8n operations are actually used, then publish one signed `parity/parity.yaml` that every later slice consumes as `parity_ids` and that S14 gates on at 100 % of `used`. Zero-usage surface is dropped, not ported (D2/R5). The retrospective reconstitutes the MSP/TOGAF lifecycle record for that measurement: charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, the project-brief and evidence outputs and the closure review.
- **Scope:** the inventory and its evidence — 1,300 rows (218 used, 295 rare, 543 unused, 244 dropped) sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08, the four surface manifests, `parity/schema.json`, `parity/SUMMARY.md` and the gate G1–G7. Out of scope is a re-measurement: the samples are dated, the live sources have moved on, and a re-measurement is not recoverable.
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26; it records the lifecycle of a measurement completed on 2026-11-08, it does not authorise new work.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S00 usage inventory (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

body.assignment: Rework S00 by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and re-publish the project-brief and evidence outputs. The architecture work is the usage inventory itself — one signed parity/parity.yaml of 1,300 surfaces sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08 — recorded retrospectively and dated 2026-11-26.
body.scope: In scope: the fr served operation set (785 operations across 616 paths), all 314 RM route decorators, the 67 Planka openapi paths, the distinct (package, resource, operation) tuples of the active n8n workflows and the four named flows conveyor.start, wip.pull, ask_fr and err.card; the evidence classes A to E and their precedence; the normalisation to P-NNNN; the classification into used, rare, unused and dropped; the schema and the gate G1–G7. Out of scope: coding-*, artifacts, worker_management, inference-router, licenses and billing_service (D12/D14); n8n flows as features, which S13 re-authors; procedure_management's 54 endpoints, carried as one SUMMARY line (D10); UI screens (S12); performance and data migration (D7).
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the pack under the #526 rework delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14; the Architecture Board reviews the seven A–D artefacts, which the rework note records as approved. The programme owner signs the inventory at sign-off: the SUMMARY carries signed_off with the reviewer, the date and the sha256 of parity.yaml, and that signature states that every used id will be built and every dropped id will not. The delivery contract 01a1ff39-4ee0-7ecc-93cc-eeaf21fb9738 is approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545, distinct from the requester 01a1e607-17d9-77d3-98d3-a43a87c4633d.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate in the plan's §7 is executable and exits 0 only when every property holds: G1 no duplicate id; G2 every id matches ^P-[0-9]{4}$; G3 every used row carries an acceptance string beginning test:, e2e: or probe:; G4 every surface appears exactly once against the union of the four manifests; G5 the manifest count reconciles with the row count of 1,300; G6 at least two Loki samples exist for the B-class used rows; G7 every dropped row's evidence begins decision: or replacement:. check-jsonschema validates parity.yaml against parity/schema.json. The rework note records the reconstituted project's own verification green: scripts/verify-project.py --project S00 --snapshot <fresh> with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96, and no P0/P1 entry for the project on the strict audit.

Retrospective matrix for S00, authored 2026-11-26 from the slice plan docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md and the rework note docs/evidence/rework/S00.md. Phase a, plateau psa, kind matrix; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d26-7573-9b0c-e0f60af92003.

Six actors on the influence, interest and engagement axes. The sponsoring group decides the tranche-0 authorisation and the exit criteria that consume the inventory. # Technology standards — usage inventory

## Metadata

Retrospective catalogue for S00, authored 2026-11-26 from the slice plan and the rework note. Phase d, plateau hld, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d26-7573-9b0c-e0f60af92003.

## Entries

Eight standards. The schema fixes the row shape with nine required keys and closed enums. The contract is a JSON array with one documented row per surface. The SQL discipline is read-only and direct on master, because a session SET through PgBouncer would poison the next client. LogQL needs a quoted host field and a positive control, and it treats query_failed as a third state. Identity is P-NNNN over a normalised surface. Classification fixes the precedence and the contradiction rule. Acceptance strings exist only on used rows. The evidence standard retains two raw samples and binds the result to a hash.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Data entity catalog — usage inventory as derivation, because each entity is held in one of these formats. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: name the formats, disciplines and instruments the inventory relies on. Scope: the JSON contract, the read-only SQL discipline, LogQL sampling, identity, classification, acceptance strings and the signed hash. # Architecture Artefact Index — S00 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Metadata

The artefact set for S00 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track (track v1): the Stakeholder map, the Driver/goal/objective, the Requirements catalog and the Solution concept at phase a, plateau psa, and the Business capability map, the Data entity catalog and the Technology standards at phases b, c and d, plateau hld. Each is an approved row with a published body dated 2026-11-22; the owner is the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and the subject is project 01a1d039-0d26-7573-9b0c-e0f60af92003.

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: Stakeholder map — usage inventory (matrix), Driver/goal/objective — usage inventory (catalog), Requirements catalog — usage inventory (catalog), Solution concept — usage inventory (diagram), Business capability map — usage inventory (diagram), Data entity catalog — usage inventory (catalog) and Technology standards — usage inventory (catalog). Each carries its own entries: six stakeholders, six drivers, ten requirements, twelve components and edges, seven capabilities, nine entities and eight standards.

## Links

The typed edges are: the driver catalogue derives from the stakeholder map; the requirements catalogue derives from the driver catalogue; the solution concept realizes the requirements catalogue; the capability map derives from the solution concept and the requirements catalogue; the data entity catalogue derives from the capability map and the solution concept; and the technology standards derive from the data entity catalogue. Every edge names another artefact of this pack, so no artefact is an orphan.

## Document

The index is the architecture-artifact page the artefact standard reads. The seven artefact documents were published on 2026-11-22 as rows 01a2020f-667e-7133-a201-fed4d14f3ac0, 01a20217-fba5-721e-980d-4e1e7363e335, 01a20233-5442-725b-8bce-1ead6655c8eb, 01a20239-5846-7654-ab36-84a47d8894f7, 01a20241-0409-76dd-be5f-e849dda60190, 01a20245-e130-703b-bb58-040abe069625 and 01a2024a-699e-723e-ab74-9eeb2af52742; this index is the retrospective page authored on 2026-11-26 over them.

risk.title: The dated samples cannot be re-measured, so a later reader cannot reproduce the counts
risk.body: The inventory was sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08, and the rework note records that the live sources have moved on and that a re-measurement is not recoverable. This retrospective row, dated 2026-11-26, records the limit instead of hiding it: the 1,300 rows and their four statuses stand as the signed record of those two windows, not as a live measurement.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: A used id that no later slice builds would break S14's 100 % gate
risk.body: The sign-off states that every used id will be built at cutover and every dropped id will not, and S14 gates on 100 % of used. The 218 used rows therefore become obligations for the slices that inherit them. This retrospective row records that a used id left unbuilt is a delivery failure at S14 rather than a defect in the inventory, so the id is not quietly reclassified after the fact.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: A surface dropped by decision may still receive live traffic after sign-off
risk.body: The plan treats an A-class hit on a decision-dropped surface as a contradiction that stops the run, and the sign-off on 2026-11-08 recorded none. This retrospective row keeps the rule live: if a caller later reaches a dropped surface, the contradiction is raised rather than absorbed, because a decision-drop outranks usage and a silent reversal would undo the rebuild's boundary.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

issue.title: Planka's database cannot evidence usage: four boards and five test cards
issue.body: The plan records the starting state as five test cards and trap 3 as an empty Planka with four boards. Row counts there are not usage evidence (D3), so Planka surfaces are classified from call sites and from the openapi path set rather than from traffic or from stored rows. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

issue.title: The execution census covers three days, so it cannot answer quarterly use
issue.body: execution_entity holds three days and 470 rows. The plan records this as trap 2 and class C corroborates only: it can show a recent execution and can never stand alone as a used row. The inventory therefore reports recent execution as corroboration and leaves older use unmeasured, which this retrospective records on 2026-11-26.

assumption.title: No active caller reaches a decision-dropped surface, so the sign-off carried no contradiction
assumption.body: The plan's precedence puts decision-drops ahead of usage and makes an A-class hit on a dropped surface a contradiction that stops the run. The 2026-11-08 sign-off proceeded, which assumes that no reachable caller hit one. This retrospective assumption, recorded 2026-11-26, states the condition under which the sign-off remains valid.

assumption.title: The two adjacent 24-hour windows represent ordinary traffic
assumption.body: The inventory rests on two Loki samples, on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08, each with a positive control above zero. The assumption is that those two days are ordinary rather than exceptional: the control proves the collector was alive, not that the traffic was typical. A rare event inside or outside the windows is outside what the inventory can see, and this retrospective records that on 2026-11-26.

dependency.title: Every later slice depends on parity_ids, and S14 gates on 100 % of used
dependency.body: The plan makes parity/parity.yaml the only list: slices reference parity_ids rather than restating surface, and S14 gates on 100 % of used. The dependency runs one way, from the inventory to the slices, so a change to a used or dropped row after sign-off would require a new signed contract rather than an edit in a consuming slice. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

dependency.title: The measurement depends on read-only access to master Postgres and Loki
dependency.body: The inventory reads the master Postgres directly as postgres, never through PgBouncer, and it reads the Loki samples through the istio-proxy logs. It depends on that access being read-only and on the samples being retained long enough to be captured twice. This retrospective row records the dependency on 2026-11-26 and notes that the run writes nothing to either.

benefit.title: Zero-usage surface is dropped rather than ported
benefit.body: The inventory measures before the rebuild, so the 244 dropped rows are surface the programme does not owe. Dropping them at the inventory rather than after a port keeps the rebuild bounded to what is used or plausibly used, which is the benefit D2/R5 names in the plan. This retrospective row links the benefit to the signed contract on 2026-11-26.

benefit.title: Every planned feature enters the rebuild with a stable id and a named acceptance
benefit.body: Each used row carries a P-NNNN id and an acceptance string of the form test:, e2e: or probe:, and every later slice consumes those ids from one list. The benefit is that a feature cannot enter the rebuild anonymously or leave it without a named check: S14 gates on 100 % of used, and the id it gates on was allocated once at the inventory. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

body.commitments: Deliver one signed parity/parity.yaml of 1,300 surfaces — 218 used, 295 rare, 543 unused and 244 dropped — sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08, so every later slice consumes parity_ids from one list and S14 gates on 100 % of used. Zero-usage surface is dropped rather than ported, the four named n8n flows are carried as a named set, and procedure_management's 54 endpoints are carried as one SUMMARY line.

The contract's own terms are the plan's §7 gate: G1 to G7 plus check-jsonschema. No waiver is recorded, and the contract does not claim a re-measurement of the dated samples.

The work runs as steps 0–14 of the plan, each at most one day and read-only, over the four application surface sets, two Loki samples, the execution census, the table counts and the Keycloak clients.

The rework note records scripts/verify-project.py --project S00 --snapshot <fresh> green with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96.

project_brief_output:
# Project brief — S00 usage inventory (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome

S00 produced one signed contract for what the rebuild owes: parity/parity.yaml holds 1,300 surfaces classified as 218 used, 295 rare, 543 unused and 244 dropped, sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08. Every later slice consumes the ids from that list, and S14 gates on 100 % of used. Zero-usage surface is dropped rather than ported (D2/R5), so the rebuild starts from measured use rather than from the full surface of fr, RM, Planka and n8n.

## Boundary

Out of scope: coding-*, artifacts, worker_management, inference-router, licenses and billing_service (D12/D14); n8n flows as features, which S13 re-authors from the same evidence; procedure_management's 54 endpoints, carried as one SUMMARY line (D10); UI screens (S12); performance; and data migration (D7). The project must not fork a second inventory: parity.yaml is the only list, and a consuming slice may not restate or re-classify a surface of its own. A re-measurement is also out of scope, because the samples are dated and the live sources have moved on.

## Reuse sources

The measurement reuses existing sources rather than a new instrument: fr backend/src/capabilities/served-spec.lock.json at fr@4a579e91d355 for 785 served operations over 616 paths; RM src/routers at rm@191086942ce5 for 314 decorators; Planka docs/openapi.json at kanban@aafb771cea4c for 67 paths; n8n workflow_entity for the active operation tuples; the istio-proxy logs for the two Loki samples; execution_entity for the execution census; pg_stat_user_tables for the fr table counts; and the keycloak client table for the client evidence.

## Inception units

The project is its own inception unit: the plan records 'Programme project: S00 · issues none yet', and the slice plan docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md is the analysis the work starts from, against SPEC sections §4, §8 S0, §9 and §11 R5. The retrospective reconstitutes the governance record over the completed measurement — charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven A–D artefacts approved by the board, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, the project brief, the evidence and the closure review — with the 38 acts recorded in transcript.jsonl.

## Dependencies

The plan records depends_on as empty, so S00 blocks rather than waits. Its dependants are every later slice that consumes parity_ids and S14, which gates on 100 % of used. Operationally the measurement depended on read-only access to the master Postgres, never through PgBouncer, and on Loki retaining both 24-hour windows. In governance it depends on the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14, the approved scope baseline 01a1ff39-8d6e-7270-b2ba-9d235eb28b83 and the delivery contract 01a1ff39-4ee0-7ecc-93cc-eeaf21fb9738.

## Acceptance

The plan's §7 gate exits 0 only when the ids are unique and shaped P-NNNN, every used row carries a test:, e2e: or probe: acceptance string, every surface appears exactly once against the manifest union, the count reconciles at 1,300, two Loki samples support the B-class used rows, every dropped row starts with decision: or replacement:, and check-jsonschema validates parity.yaml against parity/schema.json. The rework note records scripts/verify-project.py --project S00 --snapshot <fresh> green with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96 and no P0/P1 entry on the strict audit.

## Capabilities

The inventory exercises surface enumeration across four applications, call-site attribution through n8n and the reachable channels, traffic measurement over two 24-hour windows with a positive control each, identity allocation under P-NNNN, classification under the precedence decision-drop then A then B then C then D, and gate-and-sign-off binding the result to a hash and a reviewer. Each capability leaves a named artefact: the four manifests, matched.tsv, the two samples, inventory.tsv, parity.yaml and the signed SUMMARY.

## Plan

The plan is docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md, run as steps 0–14, each at most one day and read-only. The production run sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08, signed parity.yaml on 2026-11-08 and updated the programme ledger. This brief is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26: it records that run and the governance reconstituted over it, and it does not claim a fresh measurement or a wider window than the two samples support.

# Evidence — S00 usage inventory (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Claim

S00 measured which fr, RM, Planka and n8n operations are actually used and published one signed contract for the rebuild: parity/parity.yaml holds 1,300 surfaces classified as 218 used, 295 rare, 543 unused and 244 dropped, sampled on 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08. Every used row carries an acceptance string, every dropped row carries a named reason, the gate G1 to G7 and the schema check passed at sign-off, and every later slice consumes parity_ids from this one list with S14 gating on 100 % of used.

## Evidence

The contract is parity/parity.yaml with parity/schema.json, which fixes nine required keys and admits no others. The surface sets are the four manifests under parity/surfaces/: fr from served-spec.lock.json at fr@4a579e91d355, 785 operations over 616 paths; RM from src/routers at rm@191086942ce5, 314 decorators; Planka from docs/openapi.json at kanban@aafb771cea4c, 67 paths; and n8n from the active workflow tuples plus conveyor.start, wip.pull, ask_fr and err.card. The evidence under parity/evidence/ holds the two Loki samples, the execution census, the row counts, matched.tsv and the preflight. parity/SUMMARY.md carries the counts per area and status, the gate output and the sign block.

## Verification

The gate in the plan's §7 was run under bash with set -euo pipefail: G1 found no duplicate id, G2 every id matched ^P-[0-9]4$, G3 every used row carried a test:, e2e: or probe: string, G4 the manifest union and the contract agreed with no diff, G5 the count reconciled at 1,300, G6 two samples supported the B-class used rows, G7 no dropped row lacked a reason, and check-jsonschema validated the contract against its schema. The rework note records scripts/verify-project.py --project S00 --snapshot <fresh> green with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96 and no P0/P1 entry on the strict audit. This content pack is checked offline by scripts/rework-content-check.py --project S00 before the factory reads it.

## Links

The plan is docs/plans/slices/S00-usage-inventory.md, against SPEC §4, §8 S0, §9 and §11 R5. The governance record is the Statement of Architecture Work 01a1ff37-e240-779b-aab5-74a3fa86ecad, the delivery contract 01a1ff39-4ee0-7ecc-93cc-eeaf21fb9738 approved by 01a1ff39-637a-7a73-b91f-f95a02e804da, the scope baseline 01a1ff39-8d6e-7270-b2ba-9d235eb28b83, the Phase-G review 01a1ff3a-6a97-7c12-841c-1c4f803cffb6 and the rework note docs/evidence/rework/S00.md. ## Gap

Two limits are recorded and neither is closed by this pack. The samples are dated 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08 and the live sources have moved on; a re-measurement is not recoverable and is not claimed, so the counts describe those two windows and nothing later. Within those windows the measurement is bounded by its instruments: Loki covers ingress traffic for 24 hours per sample, the execution census covers three days and 470 rows, and Planka holds four boards and five test cards, so its surfaces are classified from call sites rather than from stored rows.

closure_review:
# Closure review — S00 usage inventory (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is one signed contract for the rebuild, and the acceptance the record carries matches it: parity/parity.yaml holds 1,300 surfaces classified as 218 used, 295 rare, 543 unused and 244 dropped; the plan's §7 gate passed G1 to G7 and the schema check at sign-off; every used row carries a test:, e2e: or probe: acceptance string; and every dropped row carries a decision: or replacement: reason. Against that, scripts/verify-project.py --project S00 --snapshot <fresh> is green with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96, and the strict audit on the same snapshot carries no P0/P1 entry for the project.

## Evidence

The evidence is the contract parity/parity.yaml with parity/schema.json, the four manifests under parity/surfaces/, the two Loki samples, the execution census, the row counts and matched.tsv under parity/evidence/, and the signed SUMMARY with the sha256 and the gate output. The governance record is the Statement of Architecture Work 01a1ff37-e240-779b-aab5-74a3fa86ecad, the delivery contract 01a1ff39-4ee0-7ecc-93cc-eeaf21fb9738 approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545 rather than the requester 01a1e607-17d9-77d3-98d3-a43a87c4633d, the scope baseline 01a1ff39-8d6e-7270-b2ba-9d235eb28b83, the Phase-G review 01a1ff3a-6a97-7c12-841c-1c4f803cffb6 at level compliant, and the rework note docs/evidence/rework/S00.md with the 38 acts read back one write at a time.

## Open items

One item remains and it is not closable by this pack: the samples are dated 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08 and the live sources have moved on, so a re-measurement is not recoverable and is not claimed. The item is recorded as a limit of the evidence rather than as a defect in the delivery, and it carries no owner action beyond leaving the dated record intact. Within the windows, the instruments bound what could be seen: Loki is the ingress log only, the execution census covers three days, and Planka holds test data rather than usage.

## Decision

The retrospective decision is to close on the record the snapshot carries, at the level compliant that the Phase-G review 01a1ff3a-6a97-7c12-841c-1c4f803cffb6 records, with the dated-sample limit stated rather than waived. The decision is dated 2026-11-26 and rests on the signed contract, the gate output and the green verification; it does not assert that the counts describe any period after 2026-11-08, and it does not reopen the classification of any row.
